text: 3.3 Welcome to University Podcasts. Programs made by students for students. I'm Chen Hu and this is Science with a Professor. Our subject is Technology Development and our guest is Professor Joanne Kent, expert in robotics. Thanks for coming, Professor. When we think of robots, we generally think of simple robots that clean the floor in our home or build a car in a factory. But how close are we to having robots that are like people? Well, we already have some robots that look like people and technology is developing more every day. Robots weren't used very much in the past since they were always really expensive. But because they're cheaper now, they're being used in new and interesting ways. Well, as you said, robots have been used in factories for years. Singapore and Korea are among the top five countries in the world with factory robots. And Japan has robots that serve food in some cafes. But now in the US, some restaurants are testing robots which work in the kitchen and cook food or which deliver pizza to homes. Also, robots are being developed to work on farms and help grow food. They can pick fruit, for example, or look at plant health. Interesting. But what about robots that look after or help people? Do we have those? Well, many companies are developing robots to help people who have a disability or people who can't always do housework or care for themselves easily. They might need help from robots that can carry things around the house or deliver medicine on time. These types of robots are becoming less expensive. Having a robot means people are able to stay in their own homes. So do people have a much better quality of life thanks to these new types of robots? Yes, but at this time, it's too expensive to have robots at home that can pick people up or feed them. Also, when robots were used in care homes, the nurses found that the robots didn't save time. Why is that? The robots had to be moved and watched. The nurses spent time looking after the robots, and so they had less time to look after the people. They stopped using the robots due to the lost time. I see. What are some other ways that robots are used? These days, people use robots for science research to repair equipment in the ocean and as assistance to doctors and librarians. Really? What kind of science research? I know about robots on the planet Mars. Yes, robots go to places that we can't go to collect information, like on Mars. They can prevent accidents by doing dangerous things, and they can go into areas with bad pollution. And you also said robots could be doctors or librarians. Does that mean I shouldn't study for a degree in library studies because a robot is going to take all the librarians' jobs? No, robots only help with the boring parts of being a librarian. They use barcodes to look for books on the shelves or put books in the right place. Okay. But what about a robot doctor? Am I going to see a robot when I go to the doctors? No, not yet, but doctors can use robotic arms to help them do surgery. People stay in hospital for a shorter time because of fewer problems. Well, we've heard about robots that clean your house, cook food, do research, and even help your doctor too. Okay, we have some questions coming in, so let's hear the first one.
